## Purpose
FastAPI dependency-injection functions that authenticate every protected request: decode and validate the bearer JWT, load the corresponding `User`, and enforce token revocation (both per-token logout and a blanket revocation on password change).

## Shape
- `_decode_and_load_user` — shared core: decodes the JWT, raises a generic 401 (`_invalid_token`) for any unrecoverable failure (bad signature, expired, missing subject, unknown user), returns `(user, payload)`.
- `_check_password_change_revocation` — rejects a token whose `iat` predates the user's `password_changed_at`, compared at whole-second resolution to avoid a same-second false revocation.
- `_maybe_run_lazy_gc` — ~0.1% chance per request of running `cleanup_expired_revocations`, swallowing any failure so GC never breaks a real request.
- `get_current_user_with_payload` / `get_current_user` — the standard dependencies: full revocation gate (per-jti + password-change) then return the user (optionally with the decoded payload).
- `get_user_for_logout` — a variant for `/logout` that skips the per-jti revocation check (since hitting logout twice with the same token should both report success), but still applies the password-change gate.

## Why this shape
The functions are layered (a name-mangled `_decode_and_load_user` core plus differently-gated public wrappers) so the idempotency requirement of `/logout` — treating an already-revoked token as a success, not a 401 — can be satisfied without duplicating the JWT-decode/user-lookup logic.
